text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein calls for a pan-Islamic plan to deal with modern social problems.
- Supply Ministry intervenes to bring down prices of frozen chickens by dumping large quantities at below market prices to help low income groups.

- Active contacts by the Moslem Brotherhood with other pan Arab and leftist opposition parties over coordinating positions on the boycott of the coming elections; expectations of a meeting soon between Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali and the brotherhood's leader.
- Majali departs to Malaysia next Friday to head Jordan's delegation to an international economic conference.
- Central Bank governor says foreign investments over the last six months exceeded $300 million; net foreign currency reserves topped $1.150 billion.
- King Hussein says 70 percent of refugees around the world are Moslems.
- Jordan and Kuwait to play on Wednesday a friendly soccer match in pan-Arab tournment.
- Leftist parties engage in dialogue with the Islamists; official confirmation of a coming meeting between the Brotherhood and Majali.
- Cabinet sets up a ministerial committee to handle Gulf war compensation money for Jordanian returnees.
- Government, opposition to meet in bid to soften stands before elections.
